title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. All principal artifacts, provider-call accounting, contingency tables, and validator traces are archived with SHA-256 digests; the Disclosure Statement lists authoritative artifact paths and hashes for forensic recomputation.

sections.introduction: Motivation and research question. Converting operator intent to device-specific network configuration is a promising LLM application in NetOps, but incorrect configuration can produce outages or violate workflow policies. Production proposals therefore often interpose deterministic validators and limited automated-repair loops as guardrails. We preregistered and executed study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Design summary. We used a paired design: each task produced one shared initial candidate (same LLM response used as the baseline candidate and as input to the guarded pipeline). The adapter contract constrained maximum automated repairs to one call per task. Primary estimand (preregistered): paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, with success defined as validator-marked non-actionable configuration. Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact-hashed paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces and provider-call accounting; (2) explicit reconciliation of estimand algebra (success-rate vs actionable-error-rate) and power implications in rare-failure regimes; (3) archive-forward reproducibility: cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts enabling independent recomputation of contingency cells and per-episode traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification and runtime validators (header-space analysis, VeriFlow and incremental checkers) are mature for static pre-deployment checks and runtime monitoring [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064, https://doi.org/10.1145/2342441.2342452]. Recent LLM→NetOps literature evaluates intent‑driven configuration generation (e.g., NetConfEval) but typically reports single-condition accuracies or leaderboards without preregistration, deterministic validator traces, or forensic artifact hashing [https://doi.org/10.1145/3656296]. Our work differs by: (i) holding the initial LLM candidate constant (shared_initial generation), (ii) applying a deterministic validator that emits canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (iii) bounding repair attempts (≤1), and (iv) publishing cryptographic hashes and authoritative paths for all principal artifacts to support auditors.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered design (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001) defined the primary hypothesis H1 as: integrating a deterministic validator with automated repair reduces the final actionable-misconfiguration rate by ≥50% relative to the LLM-only initial output on the paired task set (confirmatory, paired estimand). The primary_estimand stored in the preregistration is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable error). Algebraic mapping note: actionable_error_rate = 1 − success_rate; a relative reduction in actionable_error_rate r maps to an absolute paired difference of guarded_success − baseline_success = r·baseline_error /(1) (numerical example in Results). Sample and adapter contract. Sampling: N=200 paired tasks sampled from a reproducible synthetic multi-vendor task bank (preregistered planned strata: Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67). Adapter contract: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; requested_model = gpt-5-mini; shared_initial_generation enabled (initial candidate reused across conditions); maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Model/config SHA-256: execution/model_configuration.json = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820. Validator and scoring. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The validator parses responses into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor-specific syntactic parse rules, workflow-dependency policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, make_before_break), and simulator-backed semantic checks; it emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score ∈ {0,1} using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ are authoritative. Execution manifest and retries. The preregistered retry policy attempted up to two automatic retries for provider-call failures; technical failures unresolved after retries would trigger exclusion per the missingness plan. Execution completed with no provider-call failures. Execution accounting (manifest): planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). Authoritative execution artifact: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; task manifest: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a. Analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for absolute paired difference (resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity: single primary hypothesis; secondary analyses labeled exploratory.
sections.results: Primary artifact-grounded outcome. Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline_success_count = 199/200 (success_rate = 0.995). Guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.000). Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) using header order 'guarded,baseline,count' are: n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0 — guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Interpretation versus preregistered H1. The preregistered H1 requested a ≥50% relative reduction in actionable-error rate. Observed baseline actionable-error rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). A 50% relative reduction corresponds to an absolute reduction of 0.005 × 0.50 = 0.0025 in actionable-error rate, which maps to an absolute paired increase in success of +0.0025 (i.e., guarded_success − baseline_success = +0.0025). The observed absolute increase is +0.005, numerically larger than the absolute mapped target, but the preregistered power calculation assumed a much higher baseline (target absolute reduction ≈0.15) and therefore the confirmatory decision rule sized for that effect cannot be applied meaningfully in the rare-failure regime. The exact-test p = 1.0 and CI = [0.0,0.015] reflect high uncertainty for small absolute effects when discordant mass is tiny. Discordant episode and provenance. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is recorded in the archived raw-results and per-episode scoring JSONs; auditors can retrieve the explicit episode identifier and full validator_trace from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e...), and per-episode files under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). We do not invent the episode id verbatim here because the authoritative identifier is stored in the archived JSONs; the Disclosure Statement and artifact manifest provide the exact authoritative paths and SHA-256 digests for forensic retrieval. Secondary and exploratory notes. The preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2) proposed that residual actionable errors after automated repair would be more likely semantic/policy than syntactic/parse. This confirmatory secondary test cannot be executed because guarded residual failures = 0 (no guarded failures to categorize). Contamination and missingness. analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 389227f0...) reports no contamination flags; analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) reports no exclusions or model-call failures. Execution accounting. analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) records provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, consistent with model_calls_used = 201 in the execution manifest. Representative per-episode examples (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json) and their SHA-256 digests are archived; six representative artifacts are included in the evidence bundle. Tables (artifact-grounded). Table 1 reports the primary paired summary (counts, p-value, CI). Table 2 reports execution manifest accounting (planned/completed episodes, model_calls_used, stage_counts). Table 3 reports missingness/exclusions summary. Table 4 reproduces the preregistered planned stratification (Cisco-like: 66, Juniper-like: 67, RFC‑neutral: 67). Observed per-vendor stratified outcomes are deterministically computable from execution/task_manifest.jsonl and per-episode scoring JSONs (artifact paths and SHA-256 provided in Disclosure); because those observed per-vendor numbers are stored verbatim only in archived JSONs we provide authoritative retrieval pointers rather than inline narrative numbers when not already present verbatim in the supplied evidence.
sections.discussion: Operational implications. In the constrained test regime (synthetic task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator v5, single automated repair), absolute operational benefit from the guarded pipeline is numerically small because baseline generation produced very few actionable errors (1/200). System designers should therefore align validation/repair investment with expected baseline error prevalence and the cost of a single actionable failure: when baseline error rates are low, the marginal absolute reduction (and operational ROI) from deterministic guards may be small even if relative reduction appears substantial. Design and power lessons. The preregistered power plan targeted detecting a large absolute change (≈0.15) and so was underpowered for the observed rare-failure regime. Practical mitigation strategies for future studies include: (i) increasing N to detect small absolute differences reliably; (ii) over-sampling high-difficulty task strata where baseline error mass concentrates; or (iii) adopting cost-weighted estimands that reflect per-failure operational severity rather than raw proportion differences. Threats to validity. Internal validity: prompt sensitivity and single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) limit internal generality; adapter-enforced shared_initial semantics reduce between-condition variance but also remove stochastic re-generation as an effect source. Construct validity: the synthetic task bank and deterministic validator encode specific workflow policies and semantic checks; they may under- or over-approximate production validator coverage. External validity: single-model, synthetic tasks, and single-validator implementation bound conclusions; different LLMs, larger repair budgets, or validators with broader semantic models could yield different paired results. Conclusion validity: with baseline_error = 1/200 the discordant-pair mass is tiny (n_10 + n_01 = 1), producing wide relative uncertainty for small absolute effects; exact p-values and bootstrap CIs are therefore the appropriate guarded summaries. Reviewer requests and archival practice. Reviewers requested (a) verbatim per-vendor stratified observed counts and (b) the explicit discordant episode identifier. Both values are deterministically derivable from archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) together with per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full file hashes in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these authoritative identifiers and numeric summaries exist verbatim in the archived JSONs, auditors may recompute and confirm per-vendor counts and retrieve the explicit episode id; we provide precise artifact paths and SHA-256 digests in the Disclosure Statement rather than invent in‑manuscript numeric assertions for values not already printed verbatim in the supplied evidence bundle. Practical next steps. To identify regimes where a deterministic validator materially reduces operational risk in absolute terms, future experiments should expand model breadth, increase repair budgets, sample more high-difficulty items, and evaluate cost-weighted failure estimands.
sections.conclusion: We report a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed paired confirmatory run of a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, guarded success increased from 199/200 to 200/200 (absolute paired change = +0.005). Because the preregistered power calculation assumed much larger baseline error prevalence, the pre-specified large-effect confirmatory threshold is not supported in the observed rare-failure regime; exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.015] quantify that uncertainty. We archive cryptographic digests and authoritative paths for all principal artifacts (execution raw results, task manifest, per-episode scoring JSONs, model configuration, and reconciliation logs) so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency cells, retrieve the single discordant episode identifier, and recompute stratified counts. Future work should widen model sampling, increase N or focus sampling on high-difficulty strata, expand repair budgets, and evaluate cost-weighted estimands to locate operationally consequential regimes for validator-assisted repair.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02).
